questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Uniform circular motion is an accelerated motion.
2. In uniform circular motion, the speed of the body remains constant.
3. In uniform circular motion, the velocity of the body remains constant.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The speed is constant but the direction keeps changing, so the velocity (a vector) changes. A changing velocity means acceleration, here directed towards the centre.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 8 Motion
questions.h: Direction changes = velocity changes = acceleration, even at constant speed.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The slope of the distance-time graph of a body moving uniformly gives its speed.
2. The area under a velocity-time graph gives the displacement of the body.
3. The velocity-time graph of a uniformly accelerated body is a straight line parallel to the time axis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Slope of the distance-time graph is speed and the area under the v-t graph is displacement. A line parallel to the time axis shows constant velocity (zero acceleration), whereas uniform acceleration gives an inclined straight line.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 8 Motion

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The value of g is greater at the equator than at the poles.
2. The value of g on the Moon is about one-sixth of that on the Earth.
3. The value of g decreases as one goes higher above the Earth's surface.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Earth is slightly flattened, so the poles are nearer its centre and g is larger there than at the equator. The Moon's smaller mass and radius give it roughly one-sixth of the Earth's g, and g falls with height because distance from the centre increases.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 10 Gravitation

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Pressure exerted by a liquid at a point acts equally in all directions.
2. Pressure exerted by a liquid at a given depth depends on the shape of the container.
3. Atmospheric pressure decreases as one goes up from sea level.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Liquid pressure depends on depth and density and acts equally in all directions, not on the shape of the vessel. The air column above shrinks with altitude, so atmospheric pressure falls.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 10 Gravitation; NCERT Class 8 Science Ch 11 Force and Pressure

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sound travels fastest in gases and slowest in solids.
2. The speed of sound in a medium increases with a rise in temperature.
3. Sound waves in air are longitudinal waves.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Particles in solids are packed closer and pass the disturbance on faster, so the order is solid > liquid > gas. Speed rises with temperature, and sound in air travels as compressions and rarefactions along the direction of propagation.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 12 Sound
questions.h: Solid > Liquid > Gas: closer neighbours pass the jiggle faster.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The audible range of sound for human beings is about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz.
2. Bats produce infrasonic waves to detect obstacles in their path.
3. Sound of frequency below 20 kHz is called infrasound.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Bats emit ultrasound (above 20 kHz), not infrasound. Infrasound is below 20 Hz, the lower limit of human hearing, not below 20 kHz.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 12 Sound

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In myopia, the image of a distant object is formed in front of the retina.
2. Hypermetropia is corrected by using a concave lens of suitable power.
3. Presbyopia arises due to gradual weakening of the ciliary muscles and reduced flexibility of the eye lens.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: In myopia the eyeball is too long or the lens too converging, so the image falls short of the retina and a concave lens corrects it. Hypermetropia needs a convex lens; presbyopia is an age-related loss of accommodation.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 11 The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.h: Myopia = Minus lens (concave); Hypermetropia = Plus lens (convex).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A rainbow is seen when the Sun is behind the observer.
2. In a prism, violet light bends the least and red light the most.
3. Formation of a rainbow involves dispersion and internal reflection of sunlight in water droplets.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Droplets refract, disperse and internally reflect sunlight, so the rainbow appears opposite to the Sun. Red deviates the least because it has the longest wavelength; violet deviates the most.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 11 The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.h: Red bends Least, Violet bends Very much.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The resistance of a wire increases when its area of cross-section increases.
2. The resistance of a conductor is directly proportional to its length.
3. The resistivity of a material depends on its nature and temperature.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: R = rho L / A, so resistance grows with length and falls with cross-section (a thicker wire conducts more easily). Resistivity is a property of the material and varies with temperature, not with the wire's dimensions.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 12 Electricity

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tungsten is used for the filaments of electric bulbs because it has a very high melting point.
2. Nichrome is used in heating elements because it has low resistivity.
3. The wire used in a fuse has a low melting point.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Tungsten can glow white-hot without melting. Heating elements need high resistivity to produce heat (Nichrome has it and resists oxidation), while a fuse wire must melt quickly when current is excessive.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 12 Electricity

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The domestic electric supply in India is at 110 V.
2. A fuse is connected in series with the live wire of a circuit.
3. Domestic appliances are connected in series so that the same current flows through each of them.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India's household supply is 220 V, 50 Hz. Fuses sit in series with the live wire, and appliances are in parallel so each gets full voltage and works independently.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 12 Electricity / Ch 13 Magnetic Effects of Electric Current

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Magnetic field lines are open curves that begin at the north pole and end at the south pole of a magnet.
2. Closely spaced magnetic field lines indicate a stronger magnetic field.
3. Two magnetic field lines never intersect each other.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Field lines are closed curves: they run S to N inside the magnet. Their crowding shows field strength, and they cannot cross because the field would then have two directions at one point.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 13 Magnetic Effects of Electric Current

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Direct current flows in one direction only.
2. In India, alternating current reverses its direction after every 1/100 second.
3. Direct current is preferred for long-distance power transmission because alternating current loses more energy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: DC keeps one direction, and the 50 Hz Indian AC reverses every 1/100 s. AC is preferred for long-distance transmission because it can be sent with little loss of energy.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 13 Magnetic Effects of Electric Current
questions.h: 50 Hz means a flip every 1/100 s.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Convection can take place in solids as well as fluids.
2. Heat from the Sun reaches the Earth by radiation and needs no material medium.
3. Conduction is the main mode of heat transfer in liquids and gases.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Convection needs flowing material, so it occurs only in fluids. Radiation travels through empty space; in liquids and gases heat moves mainly by convection.
questions.s: NCERT Class 7 Science Ch 4 Heat

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Momentum of a body is a scalar quantity.
2. The total momentum of colliding bodies is conserved when no external force acts on them.
3. Action and reaction forces are equal and opposite and act on different bodies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Momentum is mass times velocity, so it is a vector. Conservation holds for an isolated system, and action-reaction pairs act on two different bodies, so they never cancel each other.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 9 Force and Laws of Motion

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The refractive index of a transparent medium is the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to its speed in that medium.
2. The refractive index of any transparent medium is less than 1.
3. Light travels slowest in the medium with the highest refractive index.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: n = c/v. Since light is always slower in a material than in vacuum, n is greater than 1, and the larger the n the slower the light.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 10 Light - Reflection and Refraction

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The inertia of a body depends on its mass.
2. The weight of a body on the Moon is about one-sixth of its weight on the Earth.
3. The mass of a body changes when it is taken from the Earth to the Moon.
4. Weight is measured in kilogram.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only 1 and 2 are correct. Mass is constant everywhere, and weight is a force measured in newton.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 9-10

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ultrasound can be used to detect cracks in metal blocks.
2. Echocardiography uses ultrasonic waves to image the heart.
3. SONAR uses ultrasonic waves to find the depth of the sea.
4. Sound of frequency above 20 Hz is called ultrasound.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 to 3 are correct. Ultrasound begins above 20 kHz, the upper limit of human hearing, not 20 Hz.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 12 Sound

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A convex mirror is used by dentists to see enlarged images of teeth.
2. A concave mirror is used as the rear-view mirror of vehicles.
3. A convex mirror is used in solar furnaces.
4. A concave mirror is used as a shaving mirror.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only 4 is correct. Dentists and shavers use concave mirrors (enlarged virtual image at close range) and solar furnaces use concave mirrors to concentrate light. A convex mirror gives a wide field of view and is used for vehicle rear-views.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 10 Light - Reflection and Refraction
questions.h: Convex = wide view (rear-view); concave = cave, collects (dentist, shaving, furnace).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An ammeter is connected in parallel with the component whose current is measured.
2. An ideal voltmeter has very low resistance.
3. The SI unit of potential difference is ampere.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three are wrong. An ammeter goes in series with low resistance, a voltmeter goes in parallel with very high resistance, and potential difference is measured in volt (J/C).
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 12 Electricity

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. At the extreme position of a simple pendulum, its kinetic energy is zero.
2. At the mean position, its kinetic energy is maximum.
3. Ignoring air resistance, its total mechanical energy remains constant.
4. Its total mechanical energy is maximum at the mean position.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 to 3 are correct. Energy only shifts between potential and kinetic forms, so the total is the same at all positions.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 11 Work and Energy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fleming's left-hand rule gives the direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.
2. Fleming's right-hand rule gives the direction of the induced current in a conductor moving in a magnetic field.
3. The right-hand thumb rule gives the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor.
4. An electric motor converts mechanical energy into electrical energy.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only 1 and 2 are correct. The right-hand thumb rule gives the direction of the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying wire, and a motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy (a generator does the reverse).
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 13 Magnetic Effects of Electric Current

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A passenger standing in a bus tends to fall forward when the bus stops suddenly.
Statement-II: A body in motion tends to continue in its state of motion unless acted upon by an unbalanced external force.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The lower body stops with the bus but the upper body keeps moving because of inertia, which is exactly what Statement-II says.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 9 Force and Laws of Motion

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A pencil partly dipped in water appears bent at the water surface.
Statement-II: Light changes its speed and direction when it passes from one transparent medium to another.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Rays from the submerged part bend at the water-air boundary because light travels at different speeds in the two media, so the pencil seems displaced.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 10 Light - Reflection and Refraction

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Coastal areas have a more moderate climate than inland areas.
Statement-II: Land has a higher specific heat capacity than water.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Water has a high specific heat capacity, so it warms and cools slowly and moderates coastal temperatures. Statement-II reverses this fact.
questions.s: NCERT Class 7 Science Ch 4 Heat; Ch 8 Winds, Storms and Cyclones

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
Statement-II: Sound waves in air are longitudinal in nature.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are true but Statement-II is not the reason. Sound cannot cross a vacuum because it needs a material medium whose particles are compressed and rarefied. Being longitudinal describes the wave type, not why a medium is required.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 12 Sound

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The weight of an object is the same on the Earth and on the Moon.
Statement-II: The mass of an object is the same everywhere.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Weight is mg and g on the Moon is about one-sixth of that on Earth, so weight differs. Mass is the amount of matter and does not change with place.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 10 Gravitation

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Optical device)
A. Concave mirror
B. Convex mirror
C. Convex lens
D. Concave lens
List-II (Use)
1. Rear-view mirror of vehicles
2. Magnifying glass
3. Correction of myopia
4. Solar furnace
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: A concave mirror concentrates light, a convex mirror widens the view, a convex lens converges rays (magnifier) and a concave lens diverges rays to correct myopia.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 10 and Ch 11

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Quantity)
A. Pressure
B. Power of a lens
C. Electrical resistivity
D. Specific heat capacity
List-II (SI unit)
1. ohm-metre
2. pascal
3. dioptre
4. joule per kilogram per kelvin
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Pressure is force per area (pascal); lens power is 1/f in metres (dioptre); resistivity is R x A / L (ohm-metre); specific heat is energy per unit mass per kelvin.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 8-11; NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 10, 12

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Phenomenon)
A. Rainbow
B. Blue colour of the sky
C. Sparkling of a diamond
D. Twinkling of stars
List-II (Optical principle)
1. Atmospheric refraction
2. Dispersion
3. Total internal reflection
4. Scattering
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Droplets disperse sunlight into colours; air molecules scatter short wavelengths more; a diamond's high refractive index gives it a small critical angle and repeated total internal reflection; stars twinkle due to changing refraction in the atmosphere.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 10 and Ch 11

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Component)
A. Fuse
B. Rheostat
C. Ammeter
D. Voltmeter
List-II (Function)
1. Measures current
2. Measures potential difference
3. Protects a circuit from overloading
4. Varies the resistance in a circuit
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: A fuse melts on excess current, a rheostat is a variable resistor, an ammeter reads current (in series) and a voltmeter reads potential difference (in parallel).
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 12 Electricity

questions.q:
Match the mode of heat transfer in List-I with an example in List-II:
List-I
A. Conduction
B. Convection
C. Radiation
List-II
1. Land and sea breezes
2. Heating of a metal spoon kept in hot tea
3. Heat reaching the Earth from the Sun
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Conduction passes heat along a solid, convection moves heat by currents in fluids (breezes), and radiation crosses empty space.
questions.s: NCERT Class 7 Science Ch 4 Heat

questions.q:
Arrange the following in increasing order of the speed of sound in them (at 25 degrees Celsius, as per NCERT data):
1. Air
2. Hydrogen
3. Sea water
4. Steel
Select the correct answer:
questions.e: Speed is lowest in gases (air about 346 m/s, hydrogen about 1284 m/s), higher in liquids (sea water about 1531 m/s) and highest in solids (steel about 5960 m/s). Light hydrogen is faster than air but still slower than any liquid.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 12 Sound

questions.q:
A beam of white light passes through a glass prism. Arrange the following colours in increasing order of the angle of deviation:
1. Violet
2. Red
3. Green
4. Yellow
Select the correct answer:
questions.e: Deviation increases as wavelength decreases, so the order is red, yellow, green, violet. This difference in bending is the cause of dispersion.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 11 The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.h: Red bends Least, Violet bends Very much.

questions.q: The speed of a moving body is tripled. Its kinetic energy becomes
questions.e: Kinetic energy is (1/2)mv^2, so it depends on the square of speed; tripling v multiplies the energy by 3 x 3 = 9.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 11 Work and Energy

questions.q: One kilowatt-hour of energy is equal to
questions.e: 1 kW = 1000 W and 1 hour = 3600 s, so 1 kWh = 1000 x 3600 = 3.6 x 10^6 J. This is the commercial 'unit' on the electricity bill.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 12 Electricity

questions.q: As per NCERT, taking the speed of sound in air as 344 m/s, the minimum distance of a reflecting surface from the source for a distinct echo is about
questions.e: The ear retains a sound for about 0.1 s, so the echo must return after at least 0.1 s. Sound covers 34.4 m in that time, and since it travels to the wall and back, the wall must be at least about 17 m away.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 12 Sound
questions.h: 0.1 s persistence x 344 m/s, then halve (to the wall and back) = 17 m.

questions.q: A ray of light strikes a plane mirror making an angle of 30 degrees with the surface of the mirror. The angle of reflection is
questions.e: Angles of incidence and reflection are measured from the normal, not the mirror surface. The ray is 30 degrees from the surface, hence 60 degrees from the normal, and the reflected ray makes the same 60 degrees.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 10 Light - Reflection and Refraction

questions.q: An object is placed at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror. The image formed is
o: real, inverted, of the same size and at the centre of curvature
real, inverted, diminished and between the focus and the centre of curvature
real, inverted, highly enlarged and at infinity
virtual, erect and enlarged behind the mirror
questions.e: For an object at C, the image forms at C itself, with magnification -1. The other options describe objects beyond C, at F and within F respectively.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 10 Light - Reflection and Refraction

questions.q: The power of a concave lens of focal length 25 cm is
questions.e: Power is 1/f with f in metres, and the focal length of a concave lens is negative. P = 1/(-0.25) = -4 D.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 10 Light - Reflection and Refraction

questions.q: Two resistors of 6 ohm and 3 ohm are connected in parallel. Their equivalent resistance is
questions.e: For parallel resistors, 1/R = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2, so R = 2 ohm. The equivalent is always smaller than the smallest resistor.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 12 Electricity

questions.q: Two bulbs of 60 W each are used for 5 hours a day for 30 days. The electrical energy consumed is
questions.e: Power is 2 x 60 = 120 W = 0.12 kW. Energy per day is 0.12 x 5 = 0.6 kWh, so over 30 days it is 18 kWh (units).
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 12 Electricity

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT due to total internal reflection of light?
o: Transmission of light through an optical fibre
questions.e: Twinkling arises from refraction in the atmosphere, whose layers have varying density. Diamonds, optical fibres and endoscopes depend on light being trapped by total internal reflection.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 10 and Ch 11

questions.q: In which one of the following cases is no work, in the scientific sense, done by the force named? (Assume the Moon's orbit to be circular.)
o: The force of gravity on a stone falling freely
The force applied by a girl lifting a book to a shelf
The force applied by a person pulling a trolley along the floor
The gravitational force of the Earth on the Moon revolving in its orbit
questions.e: Work needs a displacement along the force. Gravity on the Moon is directed to the centre, perpendicular to its motion along the circle, so the work done is zero.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 11 Work and Energy
questions.h: A force at right angles to the motion does no work.

questions.q: The discovery that an electric current produces a magnetic effect was made by
questions.e: Oersted noticed that a compass needle deflected near a current-carrying wire. Faraday later showed the reverse: a changing magnetic field can induce current.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 13 Magnetic Effects of Electric Current

questions.q: When a bullet is fired from a gun, the gun recoils with a velocity much smaller than that of the bullet. This is because
o: the total momentum is conserved and the gun has a much larger mass than the bullet
the force on the gun is smaller than the force on the bullet
momentum is not conserved during the firing
the gun loses more kinetic energy than the bullet
questions.e: Before firing the momentum is zero, so after firing m v (bullet) must equal M V (gun) in the opposite direction. A much larger M means a much smaller V; the forces on the two are equal and opposite.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 9 Force and Laws of Motion

questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upwards. At the highest point of its path,
o: both its velocity and acceleration are zero
its velocity is maximum and its acceleration is zero
its velocity is zero and its acceleration is g, directed upwards
its velocity is zero but its acceleration is g, directed downwards
questions.e: Gravity acts throughout, so acceleration stays at g (downward) even at the instant the ball is momentarily at rest. If acceleration were zero the ball would stay up there.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 8 Motion; Ch 10 Gravitation

questions.q: A sound wave of frequency 500 Hz has a wavelength of 0.68 m. Its speed is
questions.e: Speed = frequency x wavelength = 500 x 0.68 = 340 m/s, close to the speed of sound in air.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 12 Sound

questions.q: Planets do not twinkle, unlike stars, because
o: planets are located above the Earth's atmosphere
planets shine with reflected light, which the atmosphere does not refract
planets are much closer and act as an extended source, so the variations from many point sources average out
planets emit light of a single wavelength
questions.e: Stars are point sources and their light varies noticeably as the atmosphere refracts it unevenly. A planet can be treated as a collection of many point sources, so the dimming of some is cancelled by the brightening of others.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 11 The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.h: Stars twinkle; planets are 'many pinpoints' so they average out.

questions.q: In vacuum, red light and violet light travel
o: with a speed that depends on the intensity of light
questions.e: All colours travel at about 3 x 10^8 m/s in vacuum. The difference in speed appears only in a material medium, which is why a prism disperses white light.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 10 and Ch 11
